data.name: CONSORTIUM
data.detailed_description:
JOIN US ON DISCORD


Acerca do jogo

Game One of the iDGi-1 Trilogy.

A murder mystery, on a plane, in the future.

CONSORTIUM is an interactive narrative experience, first and foremost.

The story begins in our world - the "real world" - where we here at Interdimensional Games have developed a satellite (iDGi-1) capable of opening a digital rift through time and space. Anyone with an internet connection can travel through this rift and awaken within an alternate dimension from our own - the "game world" - in the year 2042.

  • The first of a planned trilogy, CONSORTIUM contains a fully resolvable arc entirely aboard Zenlil, it plays like a "bottle episode" of Star Trek with you being part of the cast.
  • Immerse yourself in an interactive story taking place entirely aboard the C-3800-D "ZENLIL" Consortium Command vessel on December 21st, 2042...
  • Built with a modified version of the SOURCE engine, explore ZENLIL, a living and highly interactive environment with complete freedom and agency. Includes turbulence and non-scripted decompression events!
  • Engage with a cast of over 20 people in innovative and life like conversation. Over 4,000 lines of fully voiced dialogue, each choice changes how they think about you. Or choose not to engage with them at all and never speak a word!
  • Experience an all original orchestral score by award winning composer Jeremy Soule
  • Act as detective investigating an on-board murder, while simultaneously playing peacemaker to a large band of mercenaries who seem to want YOU dead. Or play diplomacy with a smoking barrel, and let the tragedies continue to mount.
  • Dive into a world with well over 150,000 words of back-story and lore, where everything you read, see, speak, or hear relates to the story and characters, and everything is there for a reason.
  • A highly original energy based inventory system with original sci-fi weapons, gadgets and armor.
  • The story unfolds based largely on your actions. You may use diplomacy and talk your way through the entire game - never shooting anyone! OR, decide to use deadly or non-lethal force.
  • Forge lasting relationships with the crew of ZENLIL, and alter the course of the story through your actions. Your choices will change your play experience, and subsequent playthroughs offer the chance to make different decisions and see all new outcomes.
  • Regardless of what you choose to do or not, the experience always moves forward, adapting seamlessly to YOU.

reviews.review:
CONSORTIUM is one of the most ambitious and unconventional science-fiction RPGs released in the indie gaming scene, blending immersive simulation mechanics, nonlinear storytelling, philosophical themes, and first-person roleplaying into an experience that feels genuinely experimental. Developed and published by Interdimensional Games Inc., the game places players aboard a futuristic aircraft called the Zenlil in the year 2042, where they suddenly awaken inside the body of Consortium officer Bishop Six. Instead of treating the player as a standard protagonist, the narrative openly acknowledges the existence of the player as an outside consciousness inhabiting another human being. This unusual premise immediately gives the game a distinct identity and creates a constant feeling of psychological uncertainty throughout the entire experience.

The setting itself is one of the game’s strongest aspects. Humanity has supposedly moved beyond many of the political and environmental disasters of the modern era, with a global peacekeeping organization known as the Consortium replacing traditional militaries and attempting to maintain worldwide stability. However, beneath the appearance of peace and order lies a network of political tension, hidden agendas, personal conflicts, and growing paranoia. Players quickly discover that life aboard the Zenlil is far more unstable than it initially appears, especially once murder investigations, conspiracies, and conflicting loyalties begin emerging among the crew.

One of the most impressive qualities of CONSORTIUM is its commitment to player freedom. The game constantly encourages roleplaying through dialogue choices, social interactions, investigation systems, and moral decisions that genuinely alter how events unfold. Conversations are not simple cosmetic choices leading to identical outcomes but meaningful interactions that affect relationships, trust levels, and future narrative developments. Players can behave diplomatically, aggressively, sarcastically, deceptively, or passively depending on how they want to shape Bishop Six’s personality.

The dialogue system remains one of the most interesting elements of the game. Conversations happen naturally during gameplay without constantly pulling players into cinematic cutscenes, helping maintain immersion aboard the Zenlil. Crew members react dynamically to player decisions and behavior, often remembering previous interactions and adjusting their attitudes accordingly. Even casual comments can influence later situations, making social interactions feel surprisingly important. The game consistently rewards careful observation and thoughtful communication rather than brute force.

Despite taking place almost entirely within a single aircraft, the Zenlil feels remarkably alive due to the amount of detail dedicated to its crew and internal politics. Every character aboard the ship possesses personal motivations, emotional conflicts, suspicions, and hidden agendas that slowly reveal themselves through conversation and investigation. The confined setting actually strengthens the narrative because the aircraft gradually transforms into a believable social environment filled with tension and uncertainty.

The murder mystery driving the central plot provides strong narrative momentum, but the game’s greatest strengths come from its atmosphere and philosophical themes rather than dramatic twists alone. CONSORTIUM constantly explores ideas surrounding identity, morality, authority, surveillance, intervention, and the ethics of manipulating another world. Since the player technically exists as an external observer possessing another human being, the story repeatedly questions whether changing events within this universe is morally acceptable or dangerously irresponsible.

World-building is also surprisingly deep considering the game’s relatively modest scale and budget. Through dialogue, computer terminals, news articles, environmental details, and optional conversations, the game slowly constructs a future society that feels politically complicated and morally ambiguous. The Consortium itself initially appears idealistic, but deeper investigation reveals contradictions and hidden tensions beneath its utopian image. The world consistently feels larger than the immediate environment visible aboard the Zenlil.

Combat exists but intentionally takes a secondary role compared to dialogue and investigation. Players can use lethal force, non-lethal weapons, avoid violence entirely, or attempt peaceful resolutions depending on how situations develop. This flexibility strongly reinforces the immersive simulation design philosophy because the game constantly encourages players to think like real people navigating dangerous social situations rather than traditional action heroes.

The voice acting deserves praise as well. Since the majority of the experience revolves around conversations and interpersonal tension, believable performances are essential. The cast generally delivers natural and emotionally grounded performances that help sell the game’s unusual premise and philosophical tone. Characters feel like actual individuals rather than simple quest-givers or exposition devices.

Visually, CONSORTIUM clearly shows both its ambition and its independent development limitations. The futuristic architecture, holographic technology, and aircraft interiors create a strong science-fiction atmosphere, but the aging Source Engine technology occasionally struggles with stiff animations and less detailed character models. However, the strong environmental design and immersive atmosphere compensate for many technical shortcomings.

The soundtrack also contributes significantly to the experience. Ambient music and atmospheric audio create a constant feeling of mystery, isolation, and subtle tension throughout the game. Combined with environmental sounds aboard the aircraft, the audio presentation helps maintain immersion during slower investigative sections and philosophical conversations.

One of the game’s most admirable qualities is how boldly experimental it feels. CONSORTIUM clearly draws inspiration from classic immersive sims like Deus Ex and System Shock while still pursuing a highly unique identity centered around fourth-wall-breaking roleplay and player-driven storytelling. Very few RPGs attempt this level of narrative interactivity and philosophical experimentation, especially within a first-person science-fiction framework.

However, the game is not without flaws. Technical roughness is one of the most noticeable issues throughout the experience. Occasional bugs, awkward animations, unstable AI behavior, and clunky interactions sometimes interrupt immersion during important moments. Although updates improved many problems over time, traces of the game’s limited budget remain visible.

Combat mechanics also feel noticeably weaker than the dialogue and narrative systems. Shooting and movement can occasionally feel stiff or outdated, particularly during action-heavy sequences. Fortunately, combat remains relatively uncommon and never becomes the primary focus of the experience.

Pacing may also divide players. Since CONSORTIUM emphasizes investigation, conversation, and slow-burn narrative development over constant action, some sections require patience and careful attention to dialogue. Players expecting a more traditional action RPG may struggle with the game’s deliberate pacing and heavily narrative-driven structure.

For fans of immersive simulations, narrative-heavy RPGs, philosophical science fiction, and player-driven storytelling, CONSORTIUM delivers a memorable and intellectually engaging experience filled with mystery, tension, and meaningful choice. It may lack the polish and budget of major AAA immersive sims, but its creativity and ambition make it one of the more unique independent RPGs available on Steam.

Rating: 7/10

pc_requirements.minimum:
Mínimos:
  • Sistema Operativo *: Windows Vista/7/8 32bit (NO XP SUPPORT)
  • Processador: Intel Core 2 Duo 2.5GHz, AMD Athlon X2 64 2.7GHz
  • Memória: 4 GB de RAM
  • Placa gráfica: NVIDIA GTX 260 | AMD Radeon HD 4890 series
  • DirectX: Versão 9.0c
  • Espaço no disco: Requer 7 GB de espaço livre
  • Notas adicionais: Of the maximum 4GB of addressable memory space on a 32-bit system (2 ^ 32 = 4,294,967,296 bytes = 4GB), Windows reserves 2GB. This leaves any application (such as Consortium) with a maximum of 2GB to play with. During loading, Consortium can allocate up to 1.8GB worth of memory. If you are running Consortium with a 32 bit machine, be sure to close as many other simultaneously running programs as you can, otherwise "out of memory" crashes may occur.
pc_requirements.recommended:
Recomendados:
  • Sistema Operativo *: Windows 7/8 x64
  • Processador: Intel i3 2100T | AMD Phenom II x4 or higher
  • Memória: 4 GB de RAM
  • Placa gráfica: NVIDIA GTX 460 | AMD Radeon HD 5830 series or higher
  • DirectX: Versão 9.0c
  • Espaço no disco: Requer 7 GB de espaço livre
